definitions.gloss: the three wise monkeys (see-no-evil, hear-no-evil, speak-no-evil)
definitions.explanation: The famous trio of monkeys covering their eyes, ears, and mouth, representing the maxim 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil'. Most strongly associated with the carving at Nikko's Tosho-gu shrine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日光|にっこう}→日光：03515_nikkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{三猿|さんざる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{彫刻|ちょうこく}→彫刻：04448_choukoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw the three wise monkeys carving in Nikko.

examples.japanese: {三猿|さんざる}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{置|お}き{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a three-wise-monkeys figurine as a souvenir.

examples.japanese: {三猿|さんざる}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦{見|み}ざる→見る：00283_miru⟧、⟦{聞|き}かざる→聞く：00483_kiku⟧、⟦{言|い}わざる→言う：00515_iu⟧」⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{教|おし}え→教え：01909_oshie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{表|あらわ}している→表す：01868_arawasu⟧。
examples.english: The three wise monkeys represent the teaching 'see not, hear not, speak not'.

notes:
Also called ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧{匹|びき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{猿|さる}→猿：02213_saru⟧. The reading ⟦ざる→ざる：04470_zaru⟧ is a play on words: it sounds both like ⟦{猿|さる}→猿：02213_saru⟧ (monkey, voiced as ⟦ざる→ざる：04470_zaru⟧ in compounds) and like the archaic negative ending ~⟦ざる→ざる：04470_zaru⟧ ('not doing'), as in ⟦{見|み}ざる→見る：00283_miru⟧ ('not seeing').

THE THREE PRINCIPLES:
- ⟦{見|み}ざる→見る：00283_miru⟧: see no evil
- ⟦{聞|き}かざる→聞く：00483_kiku⟧: hear no evil
- ⟦{言|い}わざる→言う：00515_iu⟧: speak no evil

CULTURAL NOTE:
The most famous depiction is the 17th-century wood carving at ⟦{東照宮|とうしょうぐう}→東照宮：28793_toushouguu⟧ in ⟦{日光|にっこう}→日光：03515_nikkou⟧. The motif has Buddhist origins and spread internationally, becoming a globally recognized symbol. Often used today to comment ironically on willful ignorance.
